The hexagon [MATH: ABCDEF] is regular. Find the value of [MATH: x.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
A regular hexagon is a [MATH: 6]-sided polygon where all the interior angles have the same measure.

The sum of the measures of its interior angles is

[MATH: 180^\circ \times (6 - 2) = 720^\circ.]

Therefore, the measure of [MATH: \angle BAF] is

[MATH: m\angle BAF = \dfrac{720^\circ}{6} = 120^\circ.]

The angles [MATH: \angle QAB,] [MATH: \angle BAF,] and [MATH: \angle FAP] form a straight angle. Therefore, [MATH: m∠QAB + m∠BAF + m∠FAP|= 180^{∘}; x + m∠BAF + x|= 180^{∘}; 2x + 120^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; x|= 30^{∘}.]

Likewise, in a regular triangle, there are [MATH: 3] equivalent exterior angles, so each has a measure of [MATH: \dfrac{360^\circ}{3} = 120^\circ .]

Therefore, the given angle has the following measure:

[MATH: 45^\circ + 120^\circ = 165^\circ]
